title: Infra day playbook - capacity & network microtasks
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable personal playbook for the day — tiny tasks, reminders, and handoff-ready notes. Not polished.

Morning check (07:30-08:00)
- Slack quick-status: #infra-ops (post short line: "ok for morning checks, watching surge lanes")
- Pager queue: clear, no active GPU preempts
- Quick health commands: nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20 (spot high mem processes), kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
- Topline capacity: expected reserved pools = 220 GPUs, free usable = ~18 (watch for burst at 09:00)

Priority microtasks
1) Rebalance pool-a -> pool-b (15m)
   - reason: pool-a saturated on 8.2 GPUs, serving latency spike on t2 routes
   - quick commands: 
     - kubectl cordon node-0a && kubectl drain node-0a --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=5m 
     - move jobs with label workload=short-run via reroute script: scripts/reroute-short.sh pool-b
   - post: note node ID and time in #infra-ops, mark in ENGOPS-1423

2) Net egress rule tweak on staging (10m)
   - issue: staging batch jobs hitting rate limits to S3 region eu-west-1
   - action: open fw-rule change: allow 54.231.0.0/16 to outbound S3, test with curl to staging-batch pod
   - rollback plan: revert rule and restart kube-proxy daemonset if token errors show up

3) GPU reclaim reminder (5-10m)
   - run reclaim-lite: python tools/reclaim.py --pool=spot-preemptible --age=48h --dry-run -> inspect output -> run without --dry-run for approved items
   - flag any reclaimed nodes with label reclaimed-by=ethan and paste list in this doc

Midday sanity (12:00)
- Check slowest 5 routes in console: Console > routes > last-1h sorted by p95 latency
- If p95 > 850ms on critical routes, enable canary fallback to smaller model (see rollout: /product/rollouts/canary-guide)
- Quick note for Product: ping @Frontend-Alex if route fallback engaged

Handoff checklist (if leaving >1h)
- What I did: rebalanced pool-a -> pool-b, applied staging egress rule, reclaimed 4 nodes (IDs: ip-10-23-41-12, ip-10-23-41-13, ip-10-23-41-19, ip-10-23-41-27)
- What to watch: p95 on /generate route, queue length for batch-job-queues
- Who to call: Maya (pager), Jordan (neting)
- Quick commands to revert: scripts/revert-egress-staging.sh, kubectl uncordon node-0a

Notes & gotchas (stream-of-consciousness)
- Saw a repeated OOM on node ip-10-23-41-19 last night; suspected leak in user-training-job-22. Ticketed under ENGOPS-1450.
- If A/B rollout starts failing with kernel OOMs, try lowering batch size -> model q8_0 may still spike memory due to kv-cache fragmentation
- Reminder: update burst policy docs after today (Optimize > autoscale > burst-capacity)

Open questions / follow-ups
- Is there a scheduled capacity refresh for EU region this week? (Ping infra-capacity scheduling)
- Can we add a prefix-cache metric to console for per-route cache hit rate? Filed proposal in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/238

Quick snippets (for paste)
- Drain -> cordon -> move: 
  kubectl cordon ${NODE} && kubectl drain ${NODE} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=2m
- Check GPU process list quickly: 
  pidstat -r -u -p ALL 1 1 | grep python
- Reclaim (dry): 
  python tools/reclaim.py --pool=spot-preemptible --age=48h --dry-run

End-of-day (before handoff)
- Short log: added 4 nodes to reclamation, applied temp egress rule to staging (revert on 16:30 if no issues), rebalanced pool-a -> pool-b reducing queue wait by ~18%.
- Action items for tomorrow: finish ENGOPS-1450 root cause, follow up on console cache metric proposal, tidy up scripts/reroute-short.sh to handle multi-az

Random TODOs (low priority)
- add a one-liner in Slackbot to post current free-GPU count for oncall
- check if kpatch needs upgrade on gpu-image v2025.11.

Personal reminder: keep notes terse; if something looks like a long doc, move to shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/ and link here.
